bihar_raw_news.content: Home Judgement Scroll Down To Discover Supreme Court Supreme Court Sets Aside High Court Directions on Compassionate Appointments and Restores Government Policy of Class IV Posting. High Court's Mandate to Appoint or Promote to Class III Posts Violated Service Discipline and Government's Reservation of Class III Posts for Promotion. In Favour of Prosecution Admin 2026-09-26 08:55:08 14 Share This Article: Font size: Print Case Note & Summary The Supreme Court heard appeals by special leave arising from different orders of the High Court of Patna, where the High Court had interfered with compassionate appointments made by the Government of Bihar. The litigation concerned dependent sons and daughters of deceased government employees who died in harness and were awaiting compassionate appointments. The Government of Bihar had adopted a policy decision to appoint all such candidates to Class IV posts irrespective of their qualifications. The Co-operative Department prepared a long list of persons awaiting compassionate appointments. A committee consisting of the Secretary, Co-operative Department, Additional Secretary and Registrar was constituted to identify vacancies and recommend candidates. At the relevant time, more than 40 Class IV posts were available, and the committee recommended appointment of all candidates as Class IV employees. Twelve Class III posts were available but were kept reserved for promotion of existing Class IV employees. Some candidates who were appointed as Class IV employees approached the High Court in CWJC No. 739/1991 titled Ghidharya Devi & Ors. v. State of Bihar & Ors. The High Court by order dated August 26, 1991 directed the respondents to consider afresh their appointments to Class III posts either by promotion or fresh appointment in accordance with rules. The review petition filed by the State was dismissed after considerable delay, and appointments were directed to be made by April 30, 1992. The State did not appeal against that order, which thus became final. Following that order, similar directions were given in respect of different persons who had filed separate writ petitions. In some cases, to comply with the High Court orders and avoid contempt, the government upgraded Class IV posts to Class III posts and confirmed candidates as Class III employees. The core legal issue before the Supreme Court was whether the High Court was right in giving directions to appoint the compassionate appointment candidates afresh or promote them to Class III posts, contrary to the government's policy. The State argued that there is no vested right to a particular appointment on compassionate grounds; the policy to appoint all candidates to Class IV posts was reasonable and justified; and 12 Class III posts were legitimately reserved for promotion of existing Class IV employees. The State further argued that the High Court directions, if complied with, would convert all Class IV posts into Class III posts, violating the discipline of service. The respondents relied on the High Court orders directing appointment or promotion to Class III posts. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Cabinet Approves New Proposals Including New Universities - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Cabinet Approves New Proposals Including New Universities 26 Sep 2026 3 min read Why in News? The Bihar Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary , approved 24 proposals on 23 September 2026 , including the establishment of Maa Sita Women’s University in Patna and Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University in Begusarai . Key Points: Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University: The Cabinet approved the establishment of Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University in Begusarai . The university is proposed under the Bihar Special University Act, 2026 . Its jurisdiction will cover constituent and affiliated colleges in Begusarai and Khagaria , except institutions under Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University . Maa Sita Women’s University: The Cabinet also approved the establishment of Maa Sita Women’s University in Patna . It will have jurisdiction over constituent and affiliated women’s colleges in Patna , except those affiliated with Patna University . Livestock Farmers: The Cabinet approved the Mukhyamantri Go-Dhan Vikas Rin Yojana for livestock farmers. The scheme provides 100% subsidy on the interest component of eligible bank loans. Dairy Development: Eight dairy projects were approved for the Kosi region . The projects include the establishment of 500 new milk cooperative societies and expansion of dairy infrastructure. An estimated ₹126.07 crore has been approved for these projects. New Sugar Mill: Approval was given for establishing a new sugar mill at Warisaliganj in Nawada district . It is expected to support sugarcane farmers in Nawada, Nalanda, Sheikhpura and Jamui . Police Modernisation: The Cabinet approved ₹24.50 crore for procurement of 50 drones under the centrally sponsored police modernisation scheme. The drones will support activities such as crowd management, riverine operations, anti-Naxal operations and disaster management . Healthcare Digitisation: The Cabinet approved implementation of e-SushrutNX , developed by C-DAC , in 12 medical institutions . The system will digitise hospital processes beginning with patient registration and other treatment-related procedures. Fisheries Development: The Cabinet also approved ₹195.28 crore for transforming the Siwan Wetlands Cluster into an integrated aquaculture and export-oriented value chain under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) . bihar_raw_news.title: New Amrit Bharat Express Links Gujarat, Bihar via 20 Stations - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News New Amrit Bharat Express Links Gujarat, Bihar via 20 Stations Breaking News New Amrit Bharat Express Links Gujarat, Bihar via 20 Stations By Urban Acres September 26, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp A new Amrit Bharat Express will connect Bhuj in Gujarat with Barauni in Bihar, providing a direct rail link across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar over a 2,532-kilometre route. The service will run three days a week in each direction, according to the railway information reported by Aaj Tak Business. The train from Bhuj to Barauni will operate as train number 19427. It will depart from Bhuj at 5.30 pm and reach Barauni at 4.05 am after completing the journey. The service will run from Bhuj on Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays. The return service, train number 19428, will depart from Barauni at 11.55 pm and arrive at Bhuj at 1.15 pm. It will operate from Barauni on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays. The route will include more than 20 stations across the four states. The listed stoppages are Samakhiali, Ahmedabad, Ratlam, Kota, Sawai Madhopur, Gangapur City, Bharatpur, Mathura, Hathras, Bareilly, Izzatnagar, Pilibhit, Lakhimpur, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Siwan, Chhapra, Hajipur, Muzaffarpur and Samastipur. The service creates a direct connection between western and eastern parts of the country without requiring passengers travelling between the regions to depend on separate train services. Its route also links major rail centres in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, giving passengers access to intermediate cities along the corridor. The announcement is particularly relevant for passengers who regularly travel between Gujarat and Bihar, as well as for workers and traders moving between the four states. The route includes Ahmedabad, Ratlam, Kota, Mathura, Gorakhpur, Muzaffarpur and other regional centres, extending the reach of a single scheduled service across a wide geographic area. Barauni is an important rail location in Bihar, while Bhuj serves as a key railhead in Gujarat’s Kutch region. By connecting the two endpoints through established rail corridors and multiple state-level centres, the service adds another long-distance travel option between the western and eastern parts of India. The railway has fixed the operating days and timings for both directions. The supplied announcement does not provide a separate inauguration date or details on fares, coach composition, ticket availability or the number of services planned beyond the three weekly departures in each direction. The next operational milestone will be the commencement of the announced Bhuj–Barauni service. national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 561 India raises concerns over attacks on commercial shipping, seafarers
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has raised concerns over repeated attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Gulf, Red Sea and Black Sea, saying that the attacks were no longer exceptional occurrences. Dr Jaishankar was addressing the inaugural meeting of the ‘Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers’ during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The External Affairs Minister announced a new initiative by India and Liberia together to draw greater attention to the safety and security of ships and seafarers. He said India, a major source of seafarers, and Liberia, the world’s largest shipping registry, have joined hands to strengthen maritime safety and security. The initiative aims to establish a consultative framework to enhance maritime security and ensure that key stakeholders have a greater voice in discussions on the sector. He pointed to the recent attack on the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier MV Cape Dao in the Gulf of Oman, which left an Indian sailor dead. Dr Jaishankar also mentioned the case of the Panama-flagged oil tanker El Gaia, which was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and led to an Indian crew member being reported missing. The External Affairs Minister also drew attention to attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea, including those involving MV Omorfi and MV Golden Leo. He said these incidents could no longer be viewed as isolated cases, as commercial ships and sailors have faced a series of attacks across key waterways. He said the attacks on commercial shipping had affected people from several countries, with seafarers of different nationalities also among those killed or affected. Dr Jaishankar said attacks that disrupt maritime trade and claim civilian lives could not be defended, and called on countries to work together to stop such incidents. The External Affairs Minister is in New York, leading the Indian delegation for the High-Level Week at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly. Dr Jaishankar will address the High-Level Session today. During the visit, the Minister has attended various plurilateral and bilateral meetings.
